instructions.editing: Edit requests. Only enabled requests in enabled provider files run. product_guides contains copyable examples, not downloads. JSON requires double quotes and has no comments.
instructions.identity: id identifies the request; ticker is your label; input contains the provider identifier. Matching requests across providers need the same id, contract/instrument details and timeframe. Use a new id for a different instrument or period.
instructions.timeframe: Use lookback (for example 1mo or 1y) OR start (YYYY-MM-DD), plus end. end=null means today when run; otherwise end is YYYY-MM-DD. The requested range is inclusive. Returned raw responses are not clipped to this range.
instructions.metadata: Set product, operation, currency, unit, asset_class, description, exchange and frequency for the instrument. These fields describe the request; they do not convert the returned data.
instructions.raw_output: run.py saves original provider responses under tests/data_dumps. No local cleaning, resampling or price adjustment is applied; any provider-side adjustments are described below.
instructions.products: Use stock, etf or index with operation=price_history; use index_option with operation=option_history for SPX/SPXW. frequency=1d.
instructions.input: input.symbol is the exact Yahoo symbol, including exchange suffix/index prefix when needed. For index_option, use the full OCC identifier matching contract, for example SPX261218C07000000.
instructions.parameters: For stock/ETF/index requests use auto_adjust=false. The raw chart retains the provider close and adjusted-close fields; it is not locally adjusted. For index_option use parameters={}.
instructions.credentials: No API key is required. Yahoo is an unofficial source and availability may vary.
instructions.date_boundaries: Raw chart requests use UTC-midnight boundaries and preserve native timestamps and timezone metadata.

stock_and_etf.instructions: Copy the template into requests, verify the identifier/listing, edit dates, then set enabled=true. ETF input has the same identifier shape but use product=etf.

index.instructions: Use product=index and the exact Yahoo index symbol; confirm denomination. This is an index level, not a tradable ETF.

index_option.instructions: Raw daily option chart bars from Yahoo. No option-chain download or standardized option table is implemented.
index_option.contract: Set underlying=SPX, root=SPX (AM settlement) or SPXW (PM settlement), expiration=YYYY-MM-DD, positive strike, option_type=call or put, exercise_style=european, settlement=cash and multiplier=100. Use currency=USD. The native identifier must agree with these fields.
index_option.timeframe: The observation timeframe is independent of contract expiration. Fixed contracts do not roll automatically after expiry.
index_option.usage: Duplicate a matching request or copy the template into requests, assign an appropriate id, edit both contract and input, then set enabled=true. Option requests support download_raw() only.
